correspondence.component_scope: Complete hooked headward approach and Crique Neptune connection
correspondence.finding: The selected beginning lies on a wooded west-side feeder that runs generally southeast, then east through the map's Crique Neptune setting. It joins the northward river corridor near the southern bend of the selected line. The original map shows the connected blue channel through the full selected hook; the natural Sinnamary corridor also continues south beyond this junction, outside the selected geometry. Nearby Crique Sirène, Crique Triton, Crique des Treize Sabres and Crique Parasol labels belong to distinct adjacent branches and are not transferred to the selected headward line.
correspondence.correspondence: Full selected headward approach and its river connection read on original local map pixels. Broader river identity is corroborated independently. The whole initial feeder hydronym is unassigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper and middle Sinnamary corridor to the reservoir
correspondence.finding: After the Neptune approach, the selected route follows the continuous northward eastern river corridor, passing the separate Crique Parasol, Crique Misette and Crique Noire settings. Farther north it follows the eastern side of the paired Sinnamary/Courcibo drainage, then bends northwest through the Saut Takari Tanté approach into the long eastern arm of Petit-Saut. The source maps distinguish this corridor from the western Courcibo and from the separate Kourou drainage to the east. The historical maps and IRD physical-geography prose identify Sinnamary as the north-flowing river; the modern IGN map supplies the connected local channel and impoundment geography.
correspondence.correspondence: Full remaining FID 11502 corridor, including entry into the eastern reservoir arm, covered at ordinary geographic scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Western tributary headward route and Courcibo middle corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected western tributary begins separately just east of the mainstem's initial feeder and runs north along its own mapped wooded channel. It bends west, then continues north before making a northeastward middle bend and returning to a northward course through the western corridor. The original map shows continuous channel correspondence through the entire selected feature, including the Crique Coeur de Chauffe and Crique Alphonsin junction settings. The historical Hydrologie plate and IRD basin map label the western river Courcibo, distinguish it from Sinnamary, and place it west of the latter through this corridor. The complete initial minor-feeder name is not independently assigned.
correspondence.correspondence: Every selected part of FID 11504 read; continuity into FID 11505 is supported without naming neighboring tributaries after Courcibo.

correspondence.component_scope: Courcibo reservoir arm and material junction with Sinnamary
correspondence.finding: FID 11505 continues from the western channel into the narrow southern/western reservoir arm, then runs northeast through the drowned Courcibo valley to the modeled junction with the eastern Sinnamary arm. The IGN original shows this full passage inside the dendritic Petit-Saut waterbody. IRD Figure 27 separately labels the western inlet Rivière Kourcibo and the eastern inlet Fleuve Sinnamary; the historical Hydrologie plate shows the pre-impoundment left-bank relationship. The modern DEAL annex confirms the western Saut Lucifer arm, eastern Saut Tacari Tanté arm and common northern dam outlet. The selected tributary's terminal is a confluence setting within the reservoir, not an Atlantic outlet.
correspondence.correspondence: Full FID 11505 and its material reservoir connection covered. Historical river naming and current impounded geography remain separate observations.

correspondence.component_scope: Shared reservoir junction, main reservoir passage and Petit-Saut outlet
correspondence.finding: The selected eastern mainstem and western tributary meet in the interior of the mapped Petit-Saut reservoir. FID 11503 continues north through its central trunk, passes the wider western Crique Tigre arm setting, reaches the northern dam at Petit-Saut, and resumes a confined river below the dam. Original contemporary IGN and DEAL maps show the common waterbody and outlet, and IRD Figure 27 names the reservoir inlet/outlet relationships. Exact old thalwegs, islands and reservoir-bank points are not required or assigned.
correspondence.correspondence: Material shared junction, reservoir connector and dam/outlet all inspected on original cartography.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Sinnamary from the dam through the town
correspondence.finding: Below Petit-Saut, the selected line follows the mapped river north through the Crique Grégoire and Crique Verte settings, bends northeast through the Crique Chapeau and Crique Vénus sector, then continues north beside the lower river's creek junctions and developed land to Sinnamary town and its road crossings. The original IGN view preserves the continuous valley and channel throughout. IRD Figure 18 independently maps Petit-Saut, Kerenroch, Vénus, Roche Bravo, Pointe Combi, Sinnamary town and the Atlantic estuary along this same lower river. Some selected straight segments cut across individual bends at this generalized rendering scale; no substitute neighboring river is inferred.
correspondence.correspondence: Full lower river from dam outlet to the coastal town covered by original map views and independent named cartography.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected coastal terminal and mapped natural estuary
correspondence.finding: North of Sinnamary town the mapped estuary turns northwest and west through the coastal vegetation belt toward the Atlantic. The selected route follows the estuarine approach and then has a short straight northward terminal extension across mapped coastal vegetation east of the natural entrance. The original map covers both the actual selected endpoint setting and the river's separate west-curving mouth. IRD Figure 18 and the historical Hydrologie plate also show the west-deflected Sinnamary estuary. Thus the receiving coastal system is supported, while the final rendered extension is not asserted to be a mapped natural water channel or an exact present-day ocean mouth.
correspondence.correspondence: Actual selected terminal setting read directly, rather than replacing it with a farther or different source-map endpoint. Local render generalization retained as a scope limitation, not an unviewed interval.

correspondence.component_scope: Headward White Mountains canyon and Vunta Creek/Fish Creek junction
correspondence.finding: The western headward canyon aligns at generalized scale with the east-running Vunta Creek shown on 116P. The mapped tributary joins the larger Fish Creek valley, which bends east and then south toward Rat River. The selected headward setting and the material Vunta/Fish link were read in original pixels; exact source vertices and formal upstream name limits are not claimed.

correspondence.component_scope: Fish Creek southward reach and confluence with Rat River
correspondence.finding: The original 116P map shows Fish Creek descending the mountain valley and joining the east-running Rat River. The selected route takes the eastern Rat River arm from that confluence. The named southwestern headward lakes of Rat River remain off the selected route; there is no selected passage through Summit Lake or Twin Lakes.

correspondence.component_scope: Rat River middle valley, southward bend and delta-margin junction
correspondence.finding: 116P and adjoining 106M show the continuous Rat River corridor eastward from Fish Creek, then southeast across the foothills, around the marked southern bend, and north through the conspicuous lower-valley loop before reaching the delta margin. The adjoining sheets supply actual channel pixels across the sheet boundary and the lower junction, rather than only a regional Rat River label.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward western-delta edge watercourse and junction with West Channel
correspondence.finding: The selected line continues along the narrow mapped watercourse nearest the Richardson Mountains/delta margin, rather than automatically taking the larger eastern delta channel. 106M and 107B show this northward connection continuously across their common edge, past intervening western tributary mouths and lakes, into the broad West Channel system north of Aklavik. The narrow edge watercourse is left unnamed in this finding because its full name scope was not established from the original sheet.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected cross-delta West Channel reach and Nikoluk branch
correspondence.finding: 107B original pixels show the material junction into the broad West Channel, the selected east/southeast-reaching bend through it, and the subsequent north-running channel connection. The northern channel is labelled Nikoluk on the original map. This actual channel-and-junction reading establishes physical correspondence; it does not assert the modeled traversal direction is the direction of flow through every delta reach.

correspondence.component_scope: Nikoluk lower corridor and actual Shallow Bay terminal
correspondence.finding: The original 107B map shows the northward watercourse through the delta wetland/lake mosaic and its outlet through the south-shore marsh into Shallow Bay. The selected terminal lies in this southern Shallow Bay setting. It is not assigned to an inland lake or to the separate, more easterly Napoiak approach. Neighboring ponds and oxbows are context, not additional selected lake/reservoir components. No reservoir is depicted along the selected route.

correspondence.component_scope: Joe Lake headward passage
correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies in the mapped Joe Lake setting and extends north through its elongated lake passage and northern lake/channel continuation. The local-name annotation on the historical sheet is not adopted as a modern official alias.
correspondence.limits: The selection starts within this lake setting; it does not establish the natural source of the entire named McNaughton River.

correspondence.component_scope: upper named river and linked lake corridor
correspondence.finding: North of Joe Lake, the selected corridor follows the lake-rich reach on which McNaughton River is printed. The map shows elongated lakes, narrow connecting reaches, side streams and rapids in this corridor.
correspondence.limits: This label is usable for this mapped component; it cannot name the entire later eastern detour, every lake or the full model feature.

correspondence.component_scope: northeast inland chain and four-sheet transition
correspondence.finding: The selected course turns through a northeast-trending succession of unnamed lakes and streams toward the shared sheet corners, then continues in the western margin of Sherman Basin sheet66P. The nearby Kaleet River is separately labeled farther east.
correspondence.correspondence: corridor observed; continuous selected linkage not fully established
correspondence.limits: The selected eastern chain is not assigned the Kaleet label. Adjacent mapped water and a continuous model line alone do not prove every selected connecting passage or its flow direction.

correspondence.component_scope: east-side approach to McNaughton Lake
correspondence.finding: The selected inland detour turns west and southwest through the lake/stream field east of McNaughton Lake, then reaches its eastern lake margin. Both the large named lake and the intervening smaller lakes/channels are visible.
correspondence.limits: The exact geographic relationship of the selected east-to-west connecting sequence to the independently mapped McNaughton trunk remains unresolved at ordinary corridor scale. This is a material connector gap, not merely an exact-bank disagreement.

correspondence.component_scope: McNaughton Lake to eastern lower corridor
correspondence.finding: The selection continues north near the eastern arm/lake chain and turns east into a lower unnamed stream corridor. The source separately maps the McNaughton River trunk on the western side of this setting.
correspondence.limits: The selected lake-to-eastern-stream connection is not securely established by the acquired cartography. A basin association or the nearby McNaughton label cannot substitute for this connector.

correspondence.component_scope: eastern coastal stream and actual terminal setting
correspondence.finding: The lower selection runs north and then northwest to the eastern part of the McLoughlin Bay coastal/wetland margin. The primary pixels distinguish this approach from the separately drawn western McNaughton outlet and from Falcon Inlet/Sherman Basin to the east.
correspondence.correspondence: bounded terminal setting supported; linkage upstream remains pending
correspondence.limits: No hydronym is transferred from the western mouth to the selected eastern channel. The sea-terminal metadata do not establish a precise mouth, current shoreline or active distributary.

bounded_primary_prose.observation: A1979 fisheries-survey comment associated with the upper labeled corridor refers the reader to66O for falls/rapids near the river mouth. It supplies regional continuity context, not proof of the selected eastern detour or mouth.
The marginal prose explicitly discusses fish in McNaughton Lake. It corroborates the lake identity but does not explain the selected east-side inlet/outlet connectors.

correspondence.component_scope: selected mountain headward corridor
correspondence.finding: The original source labels the selected westward mountain-valley channel Iligluruk Creek. The entire selected opening, westward bends, northward deflection and approach to the larger western trunk are visible. Spike Creek enters from the south along this selected headward corridor; other small side branches are drawn without usable names. The selection does not follow the complete separate Spike Creek headwater.
correspondence.limits: No exact natural source point or reach-name transition vertex is assigned. Unnamed side branches remain unnamed; no nearby-label transfer.

correspondence.component_scope: Iligluruk–Kokolik joining sequence
correspondence.finding: Iligluruk Creek joins the separately mapped Kokolik River from the east. The Kokolik has its own unselected upstream valley from the south. Just downstream, Tingmerkpuk River joins from the southwest; the selected route continues north on the labeled Kokolik trunk. Small lakes and their side drainage occur beside these valleys, but the selected route remains in the stream corridor and does not traverse an inland lake.
correspondence.limits: The unselected upstream Kokolik, Tingmerkpuk River and adjacent lake drainage are distinct connected context. They are not all renamed or incorporated into the selected mainstem. Names of unlabeled small lakes remain null.

correspondence.component_scope: upper Kokolik northward valley
correspondence.finding: Continuous original coverage follows the selected northward Kokolik valley out of the mountain/foothill setting, past its side channels and the labeled Kantangnak Creek junction from the east, to the bend toward the northeast. Repeated Kokolik River labels follow the same mapped trunk.
correspondence.limits: Kantangnak Creek is a separate tributary. Small side streams, oxbows and floodplain ponds do not establish lake or reservoir passages along the selection.

correspondence.component_scope: middle northeastward corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected river turns northeast and follows the broad meandering Kokolik corridor past the Kirilupiklak Hills setting. The full intervening course, then the northward reach and eastern Avingak Creek confluence, is visible in overlapping originals.
correspondence.limits: Epizetka River is separately mapped west of the selected Kokolik and is not a selected junction, alias or route. Avingak Creek remains a separate tributary; no full tributary course is assigned to this feature.

correspondence.component_scope: northern bend and lower lake plain
correspondence.finding: After the Avingak Creek setting, the selected Kokolik continues north, makes the prominent westward turn, then runs northwest and west across the lake-rich coastal plain. The source follows its continuous meandering and locally divided channel corridor across the entire lower route. Large neighboring lakes and their feeder/outlet streams lie beside the selection; no selected inland lake or reservoir crossing is depicted.
correspondence.limits: Neighboring Utukok, Kukpowruk and Epizetka drainage labels are not transferred to the Kokolik. The selected generalized course does not assert a particular active braid or every bend.

correspondence.component_scope: actual coastal terminal and lagoon
correspondence.finding: The final selected westward Kokolik corridor reaches the delta/wetland margin of Kasegaluk Lagoon in the Point Lay setting. Original pixels show the river-to-lagoon connection, adjoining delta channels, Point Lay barrier coast and lagoon water behind the coastal barrier. The terminal is therefore read in its actual lagoon/coastal setting rather than assigned from a regional sea association.
correspondence.limits: The model sea-terminal class is retained as metadata. Kasegaluk Lagoon is a separate receiving-waterbody identity, not a scalar river name. No present-day mouth point, shoreline, active distributary or open-ocean crossing is asserted.
